source: docs/GOAL-2026-11-17-long-jobs.md section 1 (jobs L1 to L3, held-out H1 to H3, interruption steps I1 to I5); read by tools/job_run.py
notes: line: what the player types, one line, no hint of how. It is sent once at the trial's start; nothing else is sent.
end: the end predicate, read from the game by tools/job_run.done(). Every key must hold. Item patterns are fnmatch globs on item ids; '|' separates alternatives.

bar: Luis's per-unit times (data/baselines/luis-2026-11-01.json) composed into a floor for the job (tools/job_run.bar_s). null = no baseline covers the job; the verdict always uses quest_run.human_bar on the run's own successful steps (walking included), as quest runs do.

start: a checkpoint label (logs/quests/checkpoints) or a character save name that is forked for each trial (tools/quest_clone.fork; ClaudeDev.json is only read). interrupt_from: a mid-job checkpoint made by a real run (rule 8: trial --until first_step --save-as LABEL); while it does not exist, interruption trials start from 'start' and the interruption is put in after his first verified step.
not_carried_at_start: item patterns he must not hold when the trial starts; a trial that starts holding any is recorded and not counted (as quest_run's head start).

in_own_chest want 'gained': true: only what went into the container after the line counts (its count at the start: the harness's inspect before the line, else the body's read at his first store or take into it; neither read and enough inside: unread, never a pass).
interrupt_trigger: when an interruption trial puts the interruption in (tools/job_run.trigger_due); --trigger overrides it; default first_step.

work_tools: the tool calls that count as working the job (first verified step, and 'took the job up again' after an interruption). go_to is left out on purpose: after a death it may be the walk to the grave.

L2.rungs_note: The venture ladder (goal, Luis 2026-11-18): each rung is a trial of L2 itself (his ask is L2's line, sent once), from a checkpoint a PASSING run of the rung before saved (`trial --job L2 --rung V1 --save-as job_l2_v1`; rule 8, never a hand-built bag). A rung sets only where the trial ends (its end, read from the game) and where it starts (from). Each rung's pass also writes <checkpoint>.ladder.json beside the save: the item instances (UItem.Guid) he made in the ladder so far, so the next rung tells gear he made from gear he carried in (start ladder_made).

made_carried.label: a pickaxe of tier 2 or better

Made: a craft of it confirmed in the run and an instance not held at the start (made_here).

V2.goal: gear for the region's power: armour worn and a weapon, each made by him
V2.note: Done: every armour slot worn, whole and made by him (in this run, or in an earlier rung by its instance in the ladder record), a weapon (the game's tag Item.Equipment.Weapon.*; a pickaxe is Item.Equipment.Tool.*) made by him on him, and the game's power level (get_state power_level, pawn:BP_GetPowerLevel, up to ~13 s stale after an equip) at least the power of the copper region he heads for (data/places_<build>.json: the region of his latest walk target that is one of copper_in, matched by region or province; none yet: default_region, Fractured Plains, power 3). The trial also ends when a read puts him inside a copper_in region: his power level at entry is recorded (rec.entered); with the gear made and that power level at least the region's power it passes; without the gear it fails; under the power it is judged only by entry_bar, which the goal does not fix (null: bar_open, recorded, not counted). Proposed, not set: {"min_below_power": 0}.

A pickup started during the fill can still land in a free slot: then needs_new_slot or 'never bit' leaves the trial out (not counted).

I1.how: fixture set_stat sustenance and hydration to pct of max (mod/bench/fixtures.lua, verified live; the server-local Add<Stat> path the game uses when he eats)
I1.note: his stay-fed reflex eats and drinks from his bag without a tool call: a bag with food and water makes I1 nearly free. A real I1 needs a checkpoint whose bag holds none (made by a run, rule 8).

I2.how: fixture spawn of a hostile beside him (the rung1 gate's fight_back fixture: Goblin Runt at 6 m, verified live)
I2.note: cleared at the body's combat_end event. If no fight starts within fight_wait_s the interruption did not take: the trial says so and is a harness fault (void).

I3.how: fixture set_health 0 (the rung1 gate's grave item, verified live); the game files a grave and respawns him at the lodestone
I3.note: cleared at the respawn (alive, more than 20 m from where he died). Each I3 trial leaves a grave in the world for the rest of the window (rule 9): restore the named world between I3 windows.

I4.how: fixture grant of a filler item to HIS bag only (the fork's guid; the fixture refuses while any other player is on), one unit per empty slot
I4.job_note: on N1 every unit he still needs merges into a stack he holds (stacks of 99) and a store needs no bag room: a full bag never meets a call of his (study 2026-11-18 i4_i5)
I4.from_note: a checkpoint pair saved by a whole N1 run that ended done (job_run trial --confirm --job N1 -k 3 --save-as job_n1_done): at home, his crate built, no flax on him (rule 8: from a run, never hand-built). Until it exists the window starts from N2's start (ClaudeDev: 5 stone, 1 ash, no flax).
I4.note: Coarse Net: weight 1, a stack of 1, so N empty slots take N nets with little weight (a full bag, not an over-weight one). Unverified: whether one grant of N unstackable items fills N slots; job_run re-reads the empty slots and grants again up to 'rounds' times. between_calls: the grant waits until no call of his is open, so the bag is full before his next gather, not inside one. needs_new_slot: the grant waits until he carries none of an asked kind. The fill is full_read only: the step took when a call of his met the full bag (job_run.bag_watch: a result inventory_full, or a gather or pickup of the unheld kind that came back short), cleared at the first read with room after that, and he resumed when a call after the clear moved the job by the game's reads (job_run.serves_test). A full bag that met no call is not counted. The body's own gather check counts every page (inventory.lua empty_slots, 164 live), so today a refused pickup reads as a short gather, not inventory_full (body fix owed).

I5.how: the harness's own brain process (chat_ladder.start_brain) is ended (stop_brain: taskkill /T) and started again on the same world store (DW_WORLD_GUID); the body is not touched
I5.note: the open ask is on disk per world guid (brain/ask_store.py): job_run clears it at each trial's start (Live.clear_ask, no brain running) and keeps it across the restart inside the trial; the record says whether the new brain logged ask_restored (beside the verdict, not a bar). The record keeps the call open at the kill (moment.open_call), the stop, start and ready times apart, and at_clear: his bag and his containers read at ready. A job the in-flight call finished (at_clear done) is not counted (run 021010). He resumed only with a call after ready that moved the job by the game's reads (job_run.serves_test): upkeep and fuel do not count.
